title.narrative: Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises and their support systems to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative:
Between January 2022 and November 2023, Value Chain Actors and Social Partners; [Ag-Ploutos company Ltd, Ripple Effect, Federation of Uganda Employers and National Organization of Trade Unions] supported the delivery of an inclusive and integrated programme that provides farmers in sesame, cassava and soybean value chains with improved inputs, business training, access to finance and markets, including awareness raising on rights at work and mobilisation of private sector to invest in potential agricultural value chains
A financial programme involving 4 financial institutions [Equity Bank, UGAFODE, Opportunity Bank and Rural Finance Initiative] was developed in August 2022 to extend financial services to under-served refugees and host communities, operating micro, small enterprises and agricultural cooperatives. The programme uses an ILO Designed Financial Literacy Guide endorsed by the Central Bank of Uganda, in June 2022 andis in line with the Financial Inclusion Strategy for the Uganda
Business Development Service Providers Network (BSDPN), capacitated in October 2022 to provide business development services to 3,217 small- holder farmers to enhance their farming businesses, using ILO GET Ahead Enterprise Training Guide. Of these, 64.3 percent were female, 59 percent youth and 3.4 percent PWDs Through the support of the Netherlands, Ministry of Foreign Affairs funded, Inclusive jobs and education for refugees and host communities (PROSPECTS) Uganda (UGA/19/51/NLD) project, the private sector and employers received ILO technical and financial support to; 1) Create market opportunities [March 2022 to February 2023] for 1,265 farmers (689 females, 576 male; 534 refugees and 731 host community members) in West Nile farming improved sesame seed variety (E107). In addition, 40 refugee farmers, mobilised to cultivate 40 acres of improved cassava (NASE 14 variety). In Western Uganda, 1,263 farmers constituted by 378 male and 885 female of whom are 539 refugees and 724 host communities were supported through, Ripple Effect [October 2022 to April 2023] to plant 340 acres of soybean. Out of these, 495 are youths and 61 PWDs. These are part of the sesame, cassava and soybean value chain interventions, supported by ILO in refugee hosting districts, targeting refugees and host communities 2) Develop partnership [May 2022 -August 2023] with four financial institutions to extend services to under-served refugees and host communities. These were Equity Bank, UGAFODE Microfinance Limited (MDI), Opportunity Bank and Rural Finance Initiative. The financial institutions continue to receive financial support [from May 2022] to help them refine or develop products and services tailored for this market segment, in line with the Financial Inclusion Strategy for Uganda 3) Through Business Development Service Providers Network (BSDPN) from 2022 to June 30, 2023, 141 GET-Ahead trainers from 10 institutions, composed of 9 local companies under the cassava and sesame value chain and one local NGO were trained. The workshops brought together 30 participants: 15 females, 15 males, 13 refugees and 17 host community members. The GET Ahead trainers have trained 3,217 small- holder farmers to enhance their farming businesses reported above.

title.narrative: 4.2.1. Number of Member States with effective interventions to support productivity, entrepreneurship, innovation and enterprise sustainability
Output 5.3. Increased capacity of Member States to design and deliver innovative, flexible and inclusive learning options, encompassing work-based learning and quality apprenticeships

description.narrative:
In February 2022, the Ministry of Gender Labour Social Development (MGLSD) established a governance structure of the Apprenticeship Programme in Uganda by setting up the National Apprenticeship Steering Committee and the Sectoral Apprenticeship Committee. The MGLSD further in October 2022, designed two apprenticeship programmes; a scale up from ILO’s support, with support of World Bank and Belgian development agency (ENABEL) to implement apprenticeship programmes. ENABEL supported 780 new apprentices in hotel sector, with the World Bank targeting to support 9,000 apprentices in the informal sector, including in refugee host communities. Both programmes are designed by MGLSD in collaboration with employers and workers and using the governance structure established with ILO support.
In January 2023, MGLSD in collaboration with Employers under the Uganda Hotel Owners Association (UHOA) and the Training College (Uganda Hotel Tourism and Training Institute (UHTTI), the MGLSD rolled out the first quality apprenticeship programme in the Hotel Sector, benefiting 95 refugee and host community apprentices who have completed their 12-month apprenticeship training, with 68% of them retained at various workplaces. Under the support from the Netherlands, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs funded, Inclusive jobs and education for refugees and host communities (PROSPECTS) Uganda (UGA/19/51/NLD), has provided technical support to Government, Employers and Workers to implement an inclusive apprenticeship training programme targeting refugee and host community women, youth and persons with disability. From January 2022, ILO provided technical inputs and guidance to government to finalise the apprenticeship programme leading it’s roll with involvement of the workers and employer organizations in Uganda. The ILO provided technical input to the development of a workplace supervisors guide for the apprenticeship curriculum. This included technical support towards the development of the hotel assessment tool and apprentice’s logbook to track apprentices’ performance at workplace, including in June 2022, training and orientation for 50 hotel instructors. With technical guidance and support of the ILO through technical webinars and panning meetings, the Ministry of Gender Labour and Social Development in 2022 established a tripartite governance structure; the National Apprenticeship Steering Committee (NASC) and the Sectoral Apprenticeship Committee (SAC), who provided oversight and direction in the implementation of the apprenticeship programme. This technical support of the ILO and leadership of the MGLSD enabled Uganda’s technical participation in the Global Apprenticeship discussions including at the ILO Governing Board (GB) meeting on Apprenticeships in Feb 2022 in Benin and has drawn considerable attention and is designated as a flagship program by the government in the National Development Plan (NDP). The success of this program has attracted other initiatives from development partners who are financing two apprenticeship programmes with MGLSD, Uganda Hotel Owners Association and Federation of Uganda Employers with support of the World Bank and ENABEL.
